doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: King Biscuit Time and hearing Sonny Boy Williamson in Memphis
summary: He never heard King Biscuit Time but saw Sonny Boy Williamson at the Beale Street Auditorium after the Army.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I’m going to ask you a very specific question. Maybe you remember, maybe you don’t. Right around the time you got your radio, the King Biscuit Show started broadcasting...
I was just interviewing James Cotton, the harmonica player, and he said that when he was 6 years old, around 1940, he’d hear it on the radio, and he memorized Sonny Boy Williamson...
I know you’d covered one of Sonny Boy Williamson’s tunes, so I wondered if you’d listened to King Biscuit Time.
No, I didn’t listen to the King Biscuit Time show. I never heard that until later. I heard about it.
So I’m not the first to ask you this question, obviously.
Where did you hear Sonny Boy Williamson? Was it in Memphis?

I heard him in Memphis at the Beale Street Auditorium. He was on a show there. It was dancers and comedians and everything, and Sonny Boy came out by himself, and played a couple of tunes on the harmonica. I was impressed by him.
But this is when you were older, after the Army.
